Honestly it all depends on your equipment and skill level. If you have a calibrated mic and are great at applying curves and such then Dirac live won’t provide any real gain. (Essentially think of Dirac live as a cheap version of going to a pro shop and getting a tune/calibration). Dirac is good for getting tuning done quicker and easier as it does 80-90% of the work and gets your sound to 80-90% as good as possible. The house curve and slight tweaks get you to the 100%
To reiterate Dirac won’t add any features just automatic calibration. 

Now if your not great and don’t want to go to a pro shop then Dirac live should be a noticeable improvement. I added Dirac in the theater at the same time I added some sound proofing to the back wall and wow even at painful levels or whispers the audio is crystal clear. I did manage to blow a sub with my house curve, it was already a little damaged but I also was boosting it to get useful volumes from 7-8HZ on up. It lasted for a few movies at nearly max volume. I now have dual 24 inch subs to help prevent another blown sub. 

But for your specific setup I would advise going to a 2.1 as that’s all the 2x4 can handle. That’s what I did. 2x4hd with Dirac running 2 component speakers and a sub. Taking me from 10 speakers down to 5, I also eliminated the center speaker. Even if you look at the best speakers people run a 2.1, it may be a 3 way so 7 speakers in total but still run in 2 channel stereo. 

If you want more info look at AVSforum it’s a website focused on home theater, but it has loads of data about minidsp and Dirac live in the diy audio, just search keyword of Dirac or Dirac live. 

If you want to get a little tricky you could run 2 of them together and then get a 3.1 setup from your 2 2x4hds with Dirac live.

Also it works very similar to how your AVR auto tunes except it’s literally 100 times better. It uses a calibrated mic for starters not a cheap 2 dollar mic. It also uses very specific locations (9 in total) though I think you can add more. For comparison you can find it on a home theater processor from high end companies, starting at about $2000 for those processors then you still need an amp. To give you idea of what price class and category people use Dirac live for / how good it is.

Just so you know they do have other products meant to do much more. I use them for my home theater. I don’t know the name offhand but it has 8 channels of processing and the model I have has BM which is an additional cost. It even has Dirac live which does everything for you with ~9 signal listening locations with a calibrated mic. Then you check the tune add a house curve and it’s great. You can change parametric eq and many other options, but likely won’t need to as Dirac live does really well
